REUTERS/BLOOMBERG: Mexico Economy Shrinks in Q1, Beats Bleakest Forecasts
May 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Mexico's GDP contracted 0.8% in Q1. Bloomberg's headline: "Contracted Less Than Expected." But the framing leads with recession fears, not with the fact that forecasts were beaten. Finance Minister attributes the slowdown "primarily to external factors" — US tariffs and trade uncertainty.

When the US economy dips it's "headwinds." When Mexico's does — under tariffs Washington imposed — it's "stoking recession fear."

• "It opens the door for the possibility Mexico could be going through a recession"
• Finance Minister: slowdown driven "primarily by external factors" — US tariffs

REUTERS: Sheinbaum Tells Her Party Officials Should Quit If Tied to Corruption
May 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Reuters reports Sheinbaum's ultimatum to Morena: resign if involved in "anything shady." Operation Swarm has arrested 60+ officials across six states, including from her own party. That's the story — a president cleaning house inside her own movement.

Reuters frames it entirely as "amid increased pressure from the US." A Mexican president prosecuting her own party's corrupt officials is news because Washington pushed her — not because she chose to.

• "If they are involved in anything shady, they must resign and face the consequences"

AP/PBS: US and Mexico Pledge Joint Security Efforts During DHS Secretary Mullin Visit
May 21, 2026 | 🟡

📰 AP runs the Mullin visit as a "joint security" story. Mexico's actual agenda — 15 migrant deaths in ICE custody, arms trafficking flowing south, and unauthorized CIA operations on Mexican soil — gets buried under the standard cartel-and-drugs frame.

Sheinbaum described cooperation as "coordination without subordination." That framing — sovereignty as a condition, not an obstacle — is the story. AP includes it but doesn't headline it.

• Mexico filed complaints with the IACHR over migrant deaths in ICE detention
• CIA agents died operating without Mexico's authorization in Chihuahua

NYT: In Jab at Trump, Mexico Targets Foreign Election Meddling
May 22, 2026 | 🟡

📰 Mexico passes an anti-foreign-interference election law. The NYT headline calls it "a jab at Trump." When the US passes election protection laws, it's safeguarding democracy. When Mexico does it, it's a provocation aimed at Washington.

The law responds to US indictments timed near elections, threats of military intervention, and documented pressure campaigns — context the headline erases with one word: "jab." The subhead then raises "concerns about Mexico's democracy" — as if protecting elections from foreign interference undermines democracy.
